Timesheet Guide – Prasaditya IDEA Sep 30, 2026 · @Prithvi Motaparti Why this guide Everyone at Prasaditya IDEA fills a timesheet daily, one line per task, stating the result rather than the activity. As of 30 Sep 2026, no one's timesheet for the current period had been started. The entries we do have mostly describe calls, meetings and emails. The calendar, inbox, biometric machines and system audit trail already record all of that, and the lines rarely say what got done. What our recent timesheets show Recent entries across teams share five patterns. Most lines describe activity, like calls, meetings and emails, instead of what got done. The problem isn't too much or too little text. It's

activity, like calls, meetings and emails, instead of what got done. The problem isn't too much or too little text. It's the wrong text: who someone talked to, instead of what moved. Pattern What it looks like Why it's a problem Activity instead of result Lines that list calls, meetings, discussions or emails The calendar and inbox already hold this; the line says nothing about output Copy-pasted lines The same line on several days in a row No way to tell what changed from one day to the next Day total fixed first One project logged as a round number every day, the rest in odd minutes Hours were split after the fact, not tracked Repeated day The same task line and hours on two days in a row

odd minutes Hours were split after the fact, not tracked Repeated day The same task line and hours on two days in a row Unclear whether the work took twice as long or the line was reused Good lines already exist Lines that name the feature fixed or the deliverable handed over The model to follow Timesheet Guide – Prasaditya IDEA Page 1 of 6 What good practice says Good entries are short, specific and written the same day. One line per task. A timesheet is a work log, not a diary; one descriptive line per task is enough . Specific, not longer. A good entry is no longer than a bad one, just more specific . Approvable in seconds. "Coding" or "Meeting" alone tells a manager nothing; the line

han a bad one, just more specific . Approvable in seconds. "Coding" or "Meeting" alone tells a manager nothing; the line should let them approve in about five seconds. Detail matches billing. Name the service, client and period, e.g. "Bank reconciliation, Acme Ltd, March", not "bookkeeping" . Don't retype what the system logs. Trackers like Jira capture the person and the work item automatically. Fill it daily. A timesheet completed once a week from memory can't be fully accurate. The rule and the format Write the result, not the activity. Each line reads: Client/Project › Module – what got done or where it stands – hours.
